name: The Ladder: one object, every number on it

saved_from.title: Who trains your 2030 seniors (Monday 2 Nov 2026)
saved_from.approval: Krish's favourite cut; he agreed on 4 Nov 2026 that it is the Critic's first comparison (config/reference-cuts.json mon02-wide and mon02-tall, critic_first)

thesis: One object carries the whole piece, and every number is drawn on, beside or instead of a part of it, so the viewer always knows what a number is about. Krish, on the chart: "The chart makes a boring research report instantly understandable."
invariants: One through-line object for the whole piece, decided before the storyboard (spec style.idea.object); it never morphs into a different object.
One number per frame, on the object; the number that matters most takes the series colour as its underline only.
Every number carries its producer at the foot of the frame, in the mono face: PRODUCER · DATE.
Real logos appear once, at the size of a part of the object, never redrawn; a real page is shown as itself, its one line highlighted, with a slow push.
Every move means something: the object changes state to say what the voice says (a count, a thinning, a growth, marks lost or copied, a light, a line, the camera resting on a gap).
Scenes that step away from the object end by turning back into it, changed.
accent: Brand roles only, never hex: the series colour marks the most important number (underline only); mint marks only the answer (the questions and the actions). Nothing else is coloured.

layers.stage: The ink desk with the brand's grain; it does not change within a beat.
layers.subject: The through-line object (Monday: the ladder, rungs as the stages of a working life).
layers.devices: Numbers in Anton, producer credits in IBM Plex Mono, real logos and pages, the question and action cards.

signature_devices: the count on a part: a number counts down or up in one second while its part thins or grows (Monday's 27% to 9% on the junior rung)
two bars side by side, one growing to its multiple (Monday's agent hours against staff hours)
unit marks: a field of marks loses or gains some, or copies itself (Monday's 20 tellers to 13, then 43% more branches)
the missing part: the object returns with a part gone and the camera rests on the gap (the frame the cover echoes)
the line: one part lights and a line runs to another (2030's top rung to the missing junior rung)
rotate: Use one or two signature devices a beat; never every device in one beat.
captions: Word captions, one word at a time, off his face (face-with-proof default, MOTION_STANDARD); on-screen words never repeat the sentence he is saying.
sound: One sound, on the big moment only (THE_BAR ruling 11): Monday's is the drop, the count down the junior rung.
opening_and_close: The hook on his face first; one calm close, held long enough to read.
never: No figures or icons acting out a sentence; the object only ever shows a number or the gap.
No on-screen words that repeat what he is saying: a card adds the number, the producer, the date or the changed word.
No eyebrow labels, asterisks, "our read" tags or AI notes.
